title: Tenant Brand connection scope inside canonical Root Workspaces

phases.objective: Prove that personal/company remain the only canonical Root Workspace ownership modes while an optional exact Brand reference can narrow connection ownership inside either Root Workspace without widening authority or silently selecting one of multiple connections.

e2e_journeys.actor: Authenticated tenant user resolving a platform capability inside a canonical personal or company Root Workspace with an optional exact Brand scope
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The Root Workspace remains personal or company, exact Brand scope is separately authorized and bound to connection lookup, Brand child workspaces cannot masquerade as Root Workspaces, and ambiguous Brand connection sets block execution without candidate selection or leakage.
steps: Parse tenant resolve input containing canonical workspace_id plus optional brand_ref without changing the existing one-selector-workspace-v2 compatibility contract.
Resolve a company Root Workspace with exact brand_ref and verify the Brand-owned connection query binds tenant, Root Workspace, provider, owner scope and brand id exactly.
Verify a non-owner without Brand authority is denied before the connection compatibility view is queried, while an effective Brand operate grant is accepted.
Resolve an exact Brand-owned connection inside a personal Root Workspace only when the authenticated user owns that Root Workspace.
Reject a Brand child workspace id as Root connection context before Brand authority or connection lookup.
Resolve execution with two active validated Brand-owned connections and verify typed ambiguity blocks dispatch instead of selecting the first row.
assertions: Root Workspace ownership remains personal or company; Brand is an optional connection owner scope and never a third Root Workspace ownership mode.
brand_ref is accepted as an optional tenant resolve field and is passed to the resolver separately from workspace_id.
The Brand connection query binds tenant_id, Root workspace_id, provider_key, owner_scope_ref, and brand_id exactly.
Personal Root Workspace ownership is checked before Brand authority, preventing another user from using Brand scope inside someone else's personal workspace.
Tenant owner/admin Brand authority or an exact effective Brand operate-or-stronger grant is required before Brand connection lookup.
A Brand child workspace context fails closed with CONNECTION_OWNERSHIP_SCOPE_DENIED and cannot reach connection lookup.
Two eligible Brand connections return AMBIGUOUS_CONNECTION_SELECTION with candidate_count=2, no connection_id selection, and no candidate/secret leakage.
The tenant-safe ownership projection exposes Brand scope metadata but never credential payloads.
The governed generated-artifact writer materializes root OpenAPI, tenant auth OpenAPI, and frontend surface dispatch parity without widening the mutation write set.
No live database, provider, credential, Production, SQL/Migration Apply, or external mutation action occurs.
